text:
Ravi: heads up — big thunderstorm here, ~20s power flicker. my UPS kept the desktop alive but the PoE switch rebooted and my wifi AP didn't come back automatically.
Lena: ugh hate that. did the modem come back at least? sometimes DHCP takes forever.
Ravi: modem came up fine, AP was blinking amber. unplugged it for 10s and back online. zoom camera didn't reconnect so i joined audio-only for the standup.
Noah: pro tip: toggle camera in Zoom settings or switch camera off/on, feels dumb but works more than you'd expect.
Lena: also keep modem+router on UPS, not just the desktop. saves grief.
Priya: agree. travel-router + phone tether as backup is life-saving. i keep a cheap TP-Link in the closet for this.
Ravi: i actually ended up sshing into the AP on the mgmt VLAN and running a soft reboot. `ssh admin@10.0.8.2 && sudo reboot` fixed it.
Alex: lol nice. random question: did any cables get pulled/tangled? storms = cats+curiosity in my apartment.
Ravi: no pets here but my power strip is behind the desk — cable spaghetti is real. posted a pic: /files/IMG_2027.jpg — makeshift cable grommet, duct-tape safety, and my umbrella propped against the window. :cloud_with_lightning:
Priya: umbrella mount. 10/10 hacking. also, if you run a PoE switch, check for "auto power restore" in the settings so devices restart automatically after outages.
Noah: quick poll: who has a UPS >=1000VA? react with :battery: if yes.
Noah: :battery: (1000W here)
Lena: nope, <$100 UPS for modem/router only.
status-bot: power-outage event recorded for user Ravi — incident id PWR-2172. No follow-up required.
Ravi: thanks y'all — everything stable now. moving router off the floor and buying cable sleeves. will bring less duct tape next time. :raised_hands:
